items.title: Slide Hampton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: You and Paquito shared musical directorship of United Nations Orchestra? ... Yes. ... We also do some of the same things now with the Dizzy Gillespie All-Star Big Band. If I can’t go, Paquito will be the musical director...

ctx.x: It is April the 21st in the year 2006. My name is William A. Brower. I’m at the National Museum of American History along with Mr. Slide Hampton, about to begin tape 6 of an oral history. Taping the session is Ken Kimery. At the end of the – I was going towards a question that was: you’ve talked about what it meant to you, and certainly other American musicians, to have that interaction with the Latin musicians. What do you think it meant to them? And to the extent that you were in specific places like Cuba for…

They had a great admiration for the American improvisers. For American music in general, they had a great admiration. But the improvising aspect of music was what was the most interesting to them, because they were great technically. They were developed technically to a very high level. Brass players, and all of the players, especially in Cuba. They were people that had a great classical foundation in their training. So they all played the instruments very well. But improvisation was something that, in a lot of…
You and Paquito shared musical directorship of United Nations Orchestra?

items.title: Paquito D'Rivera — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Slide Hampton and myself, we were kind of musical, uh, director... We try to help putting all that together

ctx.x: After Dizzy passed you led the United Nations Orchestra for a while. Talk about that.

Well, even when Dizzy was alive, Slide Hampton and myself, we were kind of musical, uh, director—well, Dizzy was the Director, but I don’t know how to call it—musical directors. We try to help putting all that together, and then when Dizzy pass away, I conduct the band.
You made that album A Night in Inglewood.

items.title: Slide Hampton interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003
items.q: When we first played that and Paquito D’Rivera heard that he said, “God, what was that?”

ctx.x: Yes. I could not believe they pulled it off. You write some challenging music.
When we first played that and Paquito D’Rivera heard that he said, “God, what was that?”
It was a unison lick, right?
